sentences.text:
The first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 01.11.2023,
which is reproduced as below:-
1. Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.
2.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, Sri Gyan Prakash, learned Senior Advocate/ Deputy Solicitor General of India, assisted by Sri Sanjay Kumar Yadav,
learned counsel for the C.B.I and perused the record.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in Special Case No.02 of 2020, RC No.2202018E0014, under Sections 120B read with 419, 420, 467,
468, 471 IPC and Section 13(2) read with section 13(1)(d) of Anti Corruption Act,
1988 and substantive section 419, 420, 467, 468, and 471 IPC, P.S. CBI,
EOU-VI/EO-II, New Delhi with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
4.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is not named in the first information report, which was registered on 28.12.2018.
As per prosecution, the involvement of applicant was shown on the basis that he has impersonated and signed as Vijay Kumar Rohela as guarantor of the loan availed by co-accused Vishal Goyal.

The F.S.L. report has been collected by the C.B.I.
in the year 2019 but applicant was never arrested by the C.B.I. during investigation for any custodial interrogation.
It is further submitted that applicant is not a beneficiary of the alleged loan and that there is no such evidence that any loan amount has been transferred to the applicant-accused.
Further, co-accused Lakshya Tanwar and Smt. Gauri Bahl Alias Gauri Bahl and another have been granted interim anticipatory bail.

Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that there is no credible evidence against appellant and now applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 14.07.2021 and even the charges have not been framed by the trial court so far.
Learned counsel has also referred the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb (2021 Cri. L.R. (SC) 267) and submitted that in view of aforesaid facts, the applicant may be granted bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was submitted that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

5. Learned Senior Advocate/ Deputy Solicitor General of India has opposed the bail application and submitted that during investigation, it was revealed that applicant has submitted his guarantee by impersonating as Vijay Kumar Rohela and the residential property of Vijay Kumar Rohela was put as a security for loan amount of Rs.3.16 crore.
It was submitted that the main allegation in the matter is against the applicant-accused, as he has impersonated the owner of the property, which was of one Vijay Kumar Rohela.
Further, after filing charge-sheet, the applicant did not appear before the trial court and absconded and ultimately he was arrested.

It is further submitted that the applicant cannot claim parity with the interim protection Arun Nagpal vs Cbi on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131426531/
2 in anticipatory bail of co-accused, as the said anticipatory bail applications are yet to be decided on merits.

sentences.text: It was pointed out that charges could not be framed so far as the co-accused persons are absconding.
6. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

7. Perusal of record shows that co-accused Vishal Goyal, proprietor of Radhey Trading, has availed C.C. Limit of Rs.3 crore, from Central Bank of India, Wright Ganj Branch, Ghaziabad by submitting false balance sheet and forged sale-deed of the property of another person and that other accused persons were also involved in the said matter.

During investigation, it was revealed that property number SJ-53A,
Blocki-J, Sector 16, GMP Shashtri Nagar, Ghaziabad was put as security for the said loan and that applicant-accused Arun Nagpal impersonated himself as Vijay Kumar Rohela as guarantor of the loan guarantee papers by showing himself as owner of said property, which actually belongs to Vijay Kumar Rohela.
As per prosecution version, the F.S.L. report corroborates this fact that it was applicant-accused Arun Nagpal, who has signed as Vijay Kumar Rohela as guarantor on the said loan guarantee papers.

Thus, the act of applicant-accused is quite serious, as he has put the property of another person as security for the loan of Rs.3 crore and he has made forged signature of the real owner of the said property.
It appears that the public money of more than Rs.3 crore has been siphoned in a well hatched criminal conspiracy.
It was also shown that after submission of charge-sheet, the applicant-accused was being summoned again and again but he absconded and after long time, he could be arrested.

The applicant cannot claim parity with the co-accused persons, who have been granted interim protection in anticipatory bail applications, as the said anticipatory bail applications are yet to decided on merits.
In view of all attending facts and circumstances of the case, role of the applicant, amount involved in the matter, at this stage, no case, for bail is made out.
The bail application of applicant-accused is rejected.
However, if no substantial progress is made in the trial within a period of six months from today, the applicant-accused would be at liberty to file a fresh bail application in accordance with law.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is seriously ill and he is suffering from heart related serious illness.

In this connection, learned counsel has referred report of the hospital of District Jail Ghaziabad, wherein it has been mentioned that patient is suffering from "CVA/Recurrent/ N LV Function CAG- LCX 85% Stenosis LAD Distal Diffuse 80% LT. ICA 70%
Stenosis".
It is also mentioned in the report that applicant was sent to Medical College, Meerut and he remained admitted from 01.06.2024 to 11.06.2024 and that applicant is in a position of Altered sensoriam.

In discharge history of applicant issued by the G.B. Pant Hospital, Delhi, it has been mentioned that applicant is not in a position to move and to accomplish his basic daily needs and he can move only with the help of others.

It was also mentioned in the discharge summary that since last two months, his hospital attendant would help him in wearing clothes to daily activity such as Arun Nagpal vs Cbi on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131426531/
3 going to washroom, removing slipper, eating meal.
5. It is further submitted that while rejecting the first bail application of the applicant, it was directed by this Court that in case no progress is made in the trial within a period of six months,
applicant would be at liberty to file a fresh bail application.

sentences.text: After rejection of the first bail application, no progress has been made in the trial so far and even the charges have not been framed.

Lastly, it was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 14.07.2021, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

6. Learned Deputy Solicitor General of India has opposed the bail application and submitted that there are serious allegations against the applicant and the first bail application has already been rejected on merits.
However, the aforesaid medical condition of applicant could not be disputed.
7. I have considered rival submissions and perused the record.

8. Perusal of record shows that the first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 01.11.2023 and it was directed that if no substantial progress has been made in the trial for a period of six months, applicant-accused would be at liberty to file a fresh bail application in accordance with law.
It was shown that no progress has been made in the trial so far and even charges have not been framed and, thus, the trial is yet to commence.

Regarding medical condition of applicant, it has been shown that as per report of Jail Hospital, Ghaziabad, applicant is suffering from "CVA/Recurrent/ N LV Function CAG- LCX 85% Stenosis LAD Distal Diffuse 80% LT. ICA 70% Stenosis".
The applicant has remained in Meerut Medical College from 01.06.2024 to 11.06.2024 and he was also admitted to G.B. Pant Hospital, Delhi.

In discharge summary of applicant from G.B. Pant Hospital, Delhi, it has been mentioned that the applicant was not even able to identify his wife and son while he was calling their names continuously and that since 2nd June,
he is having difficulty in speech and sound slurred.

It is also mentioned in the said report that since last two months, his hospital attendant would help him in wearing clothes to daily activity such as going to washroom, removing slipper, eating meal.
From medical documents brought on record, it appears that applicant is seriously ill and he is unable to accomplish his basic daily needs without any help from other person.

9. Considering the entire facts of the matter, particularly the medical condition of the applicant,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, it would be just and proper to release the applicant on bail so he may avail proper treatment.
10.
The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Arun Nagpal involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
